>In this notebook, I present results of the pilot study run between 9^th^ and
26^th^ June 2026 via JATOS on <https://mindprobe.eu>.

```{r}
#| label: envir-feasibility
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(gt)
  library(catlasr)
})

# Search files in relation to the project repository directory, so that the code
# remains renderable no matter where is it called from
REPO <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("CATLAS.Rproj"))

# Formatting helpers shared by all manuscripts, and the tables and figures of
# this notebook (listed at the end, in "Functions used in this notebook")
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "utils-print.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "manuscripts", "forward-blocking-attention-01", "R", "02-feasibility-study.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: data-feasibility
# The three data bundles are written to the private folder
# (`CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR`) by the {catlasr} import vignette, rendered with
# `params = list(save = TRUE)`. If any of them is missing, the
# `read_private_rds()` will stop, naming the files the folder contains.
fba_imported   <- read_private_rds("fba-allergy-online-01-imported.rds")    # Before any exclusion
fba_structural <- read_private_rds("fba-allergy-online-01-structural.rds")  # Full sample
fba_screened   <- read_private_rds("fba-allergy-online-01-screened.rds")    # Primary analysis

prov <- provenance(fba_screened)

# Recruitment channel of each JATOS batch
channels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~batch_id, ~channel,
  30206L, "Family*",
  30275L, "LABELS",
  30832L, "Acquaintances",
  30829L, "Family"
) |>
  mutate(channel = factor(channel, levels = channel))

meta_imported <-
  extract_meta(fba_imported) |>
  mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
  left_join(channels, by = "batch_id")

ids_structural <- as.character(extract_meta(fba_structural)$id)
ids_screened <- as.character(extract_meta(fba_screened)$id)
ids_labels <- meta_imported$id[meta_imported$batch_id == channels$batch_id[channels$channel == "LABELS"]]

stage_labels <- c(
  stage1 = "Stage 1",
  stage2 = "Stage 2",
  stage3 = "Stage 3",
  test   = "Test"
)
learning_stages <- c("stage1", "stage2", "stage3")
n_stage <- prov$blocks[learning_stages] * prov$trial_types
```

# The experiment

The study design was identical to the @beesley2011 replication of the
three-stage forward blocking via the allergy task described in the main text.
The experimental code is recorded in the `catlaslab` repository under its
release from 19^th^ June 2026
(<https://github.com/josefmana/catlaslab/releases/tag/fba-allergy-online-01>).

::: {.callout-note title="Patch of June the 10^th^"}
The first wave of data collection (9^th^&ndash;16^th^ June), which ran on the
build preceding the patch and yielded four full data responses, included a
minor bug in debriefing variables naming that was patched for the remaining
participants. Consequently, the first four participants' data live in a
different Mindprobe instance from the rest of the sample. However, since the
code change does not affect the experimental data, data from both of these runs
are treated identically in the following text.
:::

# Participants

## Recruitment

```{r}
#| label: recruitment
n_records <- nrow(meta_imported)
n_batches <- n_distinct(meta_imported$batch_id)
n_prior <- sum(extract_meta(fba_structural)$prior_knowledge %in% TRUE)
n_prior_others <- n_prior - 1L  # My own run is among the first batch
```

Participants were recruited through `r print_num_word(n_batches, FALSE)` JATOS
batches, one per recruitment channel, including the LABELS participant pool, my
acquaintances, and my family. Together, the batches recorded
`r print_num_word(n_records, TRUE)` JATOS study results (@tbl-funnel).

::: {.callout-warning title="The author is part of the sample"}
I took part of the feasibility study myself, all while knowing the design and
its hypotheses. I answered `"yes"` to the debriefing question on prior knowledge
of similar experiments, as did `r print_num_word(n_prior_others, TRUE)` other
participant`r if (n_prior_others == 1L) "" else "s"` of the full sample.
Participants with prior knowledge stay in the primary analysis and are left out
of one of the sensitivity analyses (see [Analysis sets](#sec-analysis-sets)).
:::

## Attrition and exclusions

```{r}
#| label: funnel
rule_labels <- c(
  no_jspsych_data = "No jsPsych data",
  declined_consent = "Declined consent",
  incomplete_run = "Incomplete run",
  learning_not_reliably_above_chance = "No clear evidence of learning"
)

# Replays the exclusions recorded in provenance, in order, per channel
funnel <- count_funnel(meta_imported, prov$exclusions, rule_labels)

# The funnel must report the same number of participants as screened and
# structural bundles do
stopifnot(
  identical(tail(funnel$Total, 1), length(ids_screened)),
  identical(funnel$Total[nrow(funnel) - 1L], length(ids_structural))
)

ids_incomplete <- ids_excluded_by(prov$exclusions, "incomplete_run")
ids_learning <- ids_excluded_by(prov$exclusions, "learning_not_reliably_above_chance")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-funnel
#| tbl-cap: "Participants remaining after each exclusion rule, by recruitment channel. Rules are applied in the order listed; a participant is counted under the first rule that removes them."
tbl_funnel(funnel, levels(channels$channel))
```

```{r}
#| label: progress
# How far every participant got, read from the bundle as imported, so that the
# excluded participants are present too
progress <-
  trace_progress(
    fba_imported,
    silence = TRUE
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(meta_imported, id, channel),
    by = "id"
  )

stopped <- locate_stops(progress, ids_incomplete, stage_labels)

n_test_blocks <- sum(prov$blocks[setdiff(names(prov$blocks), learning_stages)])
partial_text <- write_partial_runs(
  progress,
  ids_structural,
  n_test_blocks
)
```

Of the runs that did not reach a complete test block,
`r print_num_word(sum(stopped$n_trials == 0L), FALSE)` ended before the first
learning trial, i.e., during the instructions or the tutorial, and
`r print_num_word(sum(stopped$n_trials > 0L), FALSE)` during the learning stages
or the test (@tbl-stopped). `r partial_text`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-stopped
#| tbl-cap: "Where the runs excluded as incomplete stopped."
tbl_stopped(stopped)
```

## Sample

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Sample characteristics of the full sample (complete runs) and of the primary analysis set (after the learning-based exclusion)."
tbl_sample(fba_structural, fba_screened)
```

## Time on task

```{r}
#| label: time-on-task
# Fixed durations of every learning trial, from `catlaslab`
# (`config/timing.js` of the `fba-allergy-online-01` release)
feedback_s <- 1.5
iti_s <- 0.5
fixed_min  <- sum(n_stage) * (feedback_s + iti_s) / 60

times <-
  progress |>
  filter(id %in% ids_structural) |>
  mutate(set = if_else(id %in% ids_screened, "Primary set", "Excluded on learning"))

duration <- na.omit(times$duration_min)
task <- times$task_min

scores_full <- score_learning(fba_structural, silence = TRUE)

timeouts <- count_timeouts(scores_full)

test_timeouts <- sum(
  extract_trials(fba_structural)$timed_out[extract_trials(fba_structural)$stage == "test"],
  na.rm = TRUE
)
```

The median run took `r print_min(median(duration))` minutes from start to end
(interquartile range
`r print_min(quantile(duration, .25))`&ndash;`r print_min(quantile(duration, .75))`,
longest `r print_min(max(duration))`; @fig-time), counting only the
`r print_num_word(length(duration), TRUE)` finished runs of the full sample,
for which JATOS records a reliable end. Responding itself took a median of
`r print_min(median(task))` minutes, and feedback and inter-trial intervals of
the learning trials add a fixed `r print_min(fixed_min)` minutes. The rest of
the run is spent on instructions, tutorials, the demography form and the
debriefing.

Every trial gave one minute to respond.
`r stringr::str_to_sentence(print_num_word(sum(timeouts$n_timed_out > 0)))` of
`r print_num_word(nrow(timeouts), TRUE)` participants let at least one learning trial
time out, `r print_num_word(sum(timeouts$n_timed_out), TRUE)` of
`r sum(timeouts$n_trials)` learning trials in total, and
`r print_num_word(test_timeouts)` test trial`r if (test_timeouts == 1) "" else "s"`
timed out.

```{r}
#| label: fig-time
#| fig-cap: "Time on task in the full sample. *Whole run* is the wall-clock duration JATOS recorded (finished runs only); the other boxes sum response times only, over the whole experiment and per stage. Each point is a participant: blue points belong to the primary set, orange points were excluded on learning. Boxes show the median and interquartile range."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
fig_time(times, stage_labels)
```

## Learning {#sec-learning}

```{r}
#| label: learning-tests
learning_alpha  <- 0.10

tests_full <- test_learning(
  scores_full,
  alpha = learning_alpha,
  silence = TRUE
)

screen_full <- screen_learning(
  tests_full,
  rule = "any",
  silence = TRUE
)

# The notebook must reproduce the exclusion recorded at import
stopifnot(setequal(screen_full$id[screen_full$exclude], ids_learning))

# Cut-offs on complete data, and the probability that a participant guessing
# throughout passes all three stages
k_stage <- compute_cutoffs(learning_alpha, n_stage)
p_guess <- prod(stats::pbinom(k_stage - 1, n_stage, 0.5, lower.tail = FALSE))

stage_tests <- count_stage_passes(tests_full)

excluded <-
  screen_full |>
  filter(exclude) |>
  left_join(
    select(meta_imported, id, channel),
    by = "id"
  )

n_failed_s3 <- sum(grepl("stage3", excluded$failed_stages))
```

@fig-learning-group shows the learning curves of the primary set. To decide
whether each participant learned, I tested,
for every participant and stage, whether the number of correct responses
exceeded what guessing would plausibly produce, with a one-sided exact binomial
test against 0.5 at $\alpha$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", learning_alpha)` over all
answered trials of the stage. On complete data, this requires at least
`r k_stage[1]` of `r n_stage[1]` correct responses in Stage 1, `r k_stage[2]` of
`r n_stage[2]` in Stage 2 and `r k_stage[3]` of `r n_stage[3]` in Stage 3. A
participant who guesses throughout passes all three stages with probability
`r sprintf("%.4f", p_guess)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-learning-group
#| fig-cap: "Learning curves of the primary set: mean accuracy per block, with error bars of one between-participant standard error each way. In Stages 1 and 2, orange marks the blocking cues and blue the control cues; in Stage 3, pink marks the critical compounds (one previously blocked and one control cue, `legit` in the data) and green the filler compounds. The dashed line marks chance."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
# {catlasr} functions are deliberately garrulous to warn about all the pitfalls
# coming with them; this is no the place for such a chat, so we suppress it
suppressMessages(plot_learning(score_learning(fba_screened)))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-stage-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Participants of the full sample whose accuracy was significantly above chance, per learning stage."
tbl_stage_tests(stage_tests, k_stage, n_stage, stage_labels)
```

Of the `r print_num_word(nrow(screen_full))` participants of the full sample,
`r print_num_word(nrow(excluded))` failed at least one stage and
`r if (nrow(excluded) == 1L) "was" else "were"` excluded
(@tbl-learning-excluded). Stage 3, the stage with the fewest trials and the
last one before the test, was failed by `r print_num_word(n_failed_s3)` of them.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-learning-excluded
#| tbl-cap: "Participants excluded on learning, with every failed stage."
tbl_learning_excluded(excluded)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Individual learning curves"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-learning-participants
#| fig-cap: "Learning curves of every participant of the full sample, one row each; participants excluded on learning are drawn in greys, dark for blocking cues and critical compounds, light for control cues and fillers. Other colours as in @fig-learning-group."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: !expr 1.1 * length(ids_structural) + 0.8
fig_learning_participants(scores_full, ids_learning)
```
:::

### Sensitivity to $\alpha$

```{r}
#| label: alpha-sensitivity
alphas <- c(0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
sensitivity <- screen_alphas(
  scores_full,
  alphas,
  n_stage,
  ids_labels
)
```

The choice of $\alpha$ sets how much evidence of learning a participant has to
give. @tbl-alpha shows the cut-offs and the participants kept at five levels.
At $\alpha$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", learning_alpha)`, the cut-offs correspond to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * k_stage[1] / n_stage[1])`,
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * k_stage[2] / n_stage[2])` and
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * k_stage[3] / n_stage[3])` correct in Stages 1 to 3,
close to the 60% criterion of @lepelley2005.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-alpha
#| tbl-cap: "Cut-offs (correct of all trials, on complete data) and participants of the full sample kept by the learning-based exclusion rule at different levels of $\\alpha$."
tbl_alpha(sensitivity, learning_alpha)
```

## Exclusion rules for `fba-allergy-online-02`

The rules below were applied to the pilot in the order listed, and their wording
is taken verbatim from the provenance record of the data, so that what is
pre-registered for `fba-allergy-online-02` is exactly what was applied here. A
participant is counted under the first rule that removes them.

```{r}
#| label: rules
#| results: asis
cat(write_rules(prov$exclusions, rule_labels), sep = "\n")
```

The last rule is decided from learning-stage data only; no test-stage response
enters it, so it is blind to the primary endpoint. None of the three published
studies closest to this design tested Stage 3 against chance: @beesley2011 and
@lepelley2007 used no learning criterion, and @griffiths2009 excluded only
participants at or below 50% correct over the final five blocks of any stage.

## Analysis sets {#sec-analysis-sets}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-analysis-sets
#| tbl-cap: "Analysis sets of the pilot. Sets 3 and 4 filter the primary set by participant metadata; they are not exclusions and are not recorded in provenance."
meta_screened <- extract_meta(fba_screened)
tbl_analysis_sets(meta_screened, ids_structural, ids_labels)
```

The primary set answers the research question; the full sample shows how much
the learning-based exclusion changes the estimates; the set without prior
knowledge removes, among others, my own run; and the LABELS set describes the
pool from which `fba-allergy-online-02` recruits.

## Implications for `fba-allergy-online-02`

```{r}
#| label: yield
n_kept <- length(ids_screened)
n_complete <- length(ids_structural)
n_rec_labels <- length(ids_labels)
n_kept_labels <- sum(ids_screened %in% ids_labels)
starts_per_kept <- n_records / n_kept
starts_per_kept_low <- 1 / stats::binom.test(n_kept, n_records)$conf.int[1]
```

Of all JATOS records, `r print_n_pct(n_kept, n_records)` entered the primary
analysis (`r print_ci_pct(n_kept, n_records)`); of the complete runs,
`r print_n_pct(n_kept, n_complete)` (`r print_ci_pct(n_kept, n_complete)`). In
the LABELS batch alone, `r print_n_pct(n_kept_labels, n_rec_labels)` of records
were analysed. Because `fba-allergy-online-02` is powered for participants
whose data survive the exclusion rules, every analysed participant takes about
`r sprintf("%.1f", starts_per_kept)` started runs, and up to
`r sprintf("%.1f", starts_per_kept_low)` at the lower end of the confidence
interval. The pilot sample was small and drawn partly from my family
and acquaintances, so these figures are a rough guide for the sampling plan
rather than a forecast.
